raw_case_text: The male patient was born on June 6, 1960, in Acaua municipality, Piaui State, was a married and was diagnosed with kala-azar in January 2014 and had a negative serology to HIV. Since then, he evolved with recurrent pancytopenia, persistent splenomegaly and a history of five previous hospitalizations at the IDTNP for the kala-azar treatment. After unsuccessful attempts with all the existing drug treatments against kala-azar, such as pentavalent antimony (glucantime, 20 mg of Sb + 5 kg/d for 30 d at first hospitalization) and liposomal amphotericin B (for 14 d at a dose of 3 mg/kg/d, in three hospitalizations), and in the face of an evolution with hypersplenism, clinical and laboratory repercussions, the patient was admitted in July 2015 to undergo a splenectomy, and at that time, on the physical examination, he presented with a palpable spleen at 12 cm from the left costal margin. In the preoperative period, an ultrasound of the abdomen was performed showing an enlarged spleen extending to the left iliac fossa. CBC with Hb 8.7 g/dL; Ht 27.9%; leukocytes 1,090/microL and 155,000/microL platelets. He underwent splenectomy on August 04, 2015, progressing uneventfully in the intra and postoperative periods. The surgical specimen measured 19.5 x 14.5 x 6 cm and weighed 1,066g (Figures 1 and 2). The histopathological study confirmed the presence of Leihmania parasites within the splenic parenchyma. He also had 7 d of liposomal amphotericin B during hospitalization. In the outpatient follow-up, cholelithiasis was identified, which became symptomatic and the patient underwent, a video cholecystectomy surgery on November 03, 2017, performed by the same team of the splenectomy, also evolving without complications. Nowadays, he has been followed-up at the outpatient clinic, for more than 4 years after the surgery, remaining asymptomatic, without further hospitalizations due to kala-azar or medications, and with a normal hematological profile.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 55-year-old male with recurrent visceral leishmaniasis and refractory hypersplenism presented for scheduled therapeutic splenectomy.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient is a 55-year-old male diagnosed with visceral leishmaniasis in January 2014 who experienced recurrent pancytopenia, persistent splenomegaly, and five hospitalizations at IDTNP for antileishmanial therapy. Despite multiple courses of pentavalent antimony and liposomal amphotericin B, he developed progressive hypersplenism and refractory cytopenias, prompting admission in July 2015 for therapeutic splenectomy.
subjective.past_medical_history: Recurrent visceral leishmaniasis diagnosed in 2014 with five prior hospitalizations; treated with pentavalent antimony (Glucantime 20 mg Sb5+/kg/day for 30 days) and liposomal amphotericin B (3 mg/kg/day for 14 days across three hospitalizations). Negative HIV serology. Origin: Acaua municipality, Piaui State, Brazil.
subjective.review_of_systems: Abdominal fullness, fatigue, chronic left upper quadrant heaviness. Home medications and allergies: None documented.

objective.physical_examination: Abdominal examination revealed massive splenomegaly with a palpable spleen extending 12 cm below the left costal margin.
objective.routine_investigations: Preoperative complete blood count: Hemoglobin: 8.7 g/dL; Hematocrit: 27.9%; Leukocyte count: 1,090/microL; Platelet count: 155,000/microL. Abdominal ultrasound: massive splenomegaly extending into the left iliac fossa. HIV serology: negative.
objective.advanced_workup: Splenectomy surgical specimen: spleen measured 19.5 x 14.5 x 6 cm and weighed 1,066 g. Histopathological examination of splenic parenchyma: performed.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Drug-resistant, relapsing visceral leishmaniasis (kala-azar) with severe secondary hypersplenism.
Diagnostic confirmation: Histopathological examination of the surgical specimen confirmed the presence of Leishmania parasites within the splenic parenchyma.
Differentials ruled out: HIV co-infection (negative serology) and primary hematologic malignancies.
Treatment and clinical course: Underwent successful open splenectomy on August 4, 2015, with an uneventful postoperative recovery, alongside a 7-day inpatient course of liposomal amphotericin B. Hematological counts completely normalized. In November 2017, he underwent elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy for symptomatic cholelithiasis without complications. At greater than four years of outpatient follow-up, he remains entirely asymptomatic with normal hematological indices and no further leishmaniasis relapse.
